I was really left unimpressed with most of the offerings. I suppose in retrospect I should not have been surprised, what would naturally be shown at these conferences would be the big "AAA" western titles. I guess for me "AAA Western" games are starting to look and feel creatively empty. And a good portion of what Sony showed seemed to all follow similar themes.

Starting with Uncharted: Non-Nathan Drake edition to Horizon DLC, and then into Days Gone (which was the most overstayed demo of E3 so far), it was nothing but Third-person over-the-shoulder games with sneaking around, ducking and shooting. I swear the three bled into each other, and I was feeling like I lost track where one game ended and the next one began.

Ok, Shadow of the Colossus remake was unexpected, but i've played that game so many times now, and I think some of the "HD" visuals are kind of not capturing the visuals of the original well, particularly the rendering. And the remake is being handled by an American studio.

Detroit? Eh, nothing compelling, and godawful dialog, I guess David Cage games still get funding somehow. And the VR stuff was just a time waster.

God of War was probably the only game that caught my eye. But for some reason something about the visuals of that games just feel "off" to me. I can't be sure to describe it, but it seemed like there was a bit of a "Cartoon"-ish vibe to the aesthetic. Also not yet feeling the monster and creature designs.

And SpiderMan holds no interest to me in the slightest. But I'm so burned out on Superheroes.

I was actually surprised that there was so little presence from Japanese developers. Capcom being the only one there showing Monster Hunter and Marvel vs. Capcom. But otherwise nothing.

EDIT: Finally. I think overall, this E3 proved that Press Conferences are no longer enticing or exciting. I actually think Nintendo has the right idea just to show video. Each Conference, including Sony's could have just been a video and it'd be distilled better. The conference crowds no longer add anything to the experience.
